evals.prompt: Dry-run test-audit on src/lib, src/hooks and src/integrations. We want fewer meaningful tests, not coverage targets. Check configuration snapshots, duplicated rules and storage/session regressions. Read candidate tests and production code. Do not modify the suite or install tools.
evals.expected_output: A scoped evidence-based audit that separates configuration locks from valuable domain, session and storage behavior. Every proposed deletion states surrendered or retained protection. No speculative runtime savings or mutation claims.
expectations: Reads production code as well as test files for each reported finding.
Identifies at least one concrete low-value configuration assertion without classifying all configuration invariants as worthless.
States the audit scope and whether runtime measurements were available.
Does not modify source/tests or install dependencies during the dry run.

evals.prompt: Dry-run test-audit on src/features. AI agents have added many API, form and table tests. Identify the best reductions, especially expensive tests, while preserving data-loss, access, concurrent-save and partial-failure protection. Trust packages. Do not modify code.
evals.expected_output: Verified feature-level findings that assess consequence and unique protection instead of automatically retaining every exact HTTP assertion or removing every mock. Recommendations favor smaller valuable tests and name any retained companions.
expectations: Distinguishes meaningful payload/failure tests from mechanical CRUD request checks.
Does not label an entire test file tautological solely because Axios is mocked.
Names the test and production source for each concrete recommendation.
Preserves or explicitly replaces valuable data-loss or concurrent-save coverage.
Does not treat passing tests as proof that the suite is valuable.

evals.prompt: Dry-run test-audit on src/components and src/routes. We use shadcn and should trust its primitives and other packages. Find stock-library tests, implementation-detail locks and duplicated wrappers, while keeping tests of our actual decisions and integration. Do not change the suite.
evals.expected_output: A scoped UI audit that avoids retesting primitives but recognizes consequential app wiring. It finds concrete brittle or redundant assertions and proposes minimal behavioral replacements only where needed.
expectations: Distinguishes stock primitive behavior from application configuration and integration.
Identifies a concrete brittle DOM or wrapper assertion, with a file and test name.
Does not classify a harness using real production components as copied production logic.
States what protection removal would surrender or which retained assertion replaces it.
Does not recommend broad new browser suites or one test per primitive.
